arms.observed: PARTIALLY_CONFIRMED. Both strategies reach 95% threshold at Phase 1 eval 3 (identical for TPE and LHS, since Phase 1 is the same). Phase 2 improvement window is tiny: Phase 1 score 0.1755 vs optimal 0.176474 = 0.55% gap. TPE finds improvement (round-robin routing) at evals 20, 33, 12 for seeds 42, 123, 456. LHS finds improvement at evals 32, 10, 33 for seeds 42, 123, 456. TPE wins on 2/3 seeds (42, 456) with advantages of 12 and 21 evals respectively. LHS wins on seed 123 by 23 evals. Average: TPE slightly faster but highly seed-dependent. MECHANISM MISMATCH: prediction said TPE learns batch-size dominance (26% range). In practice, Phase 1 already fixes batch=512. The actual Phase 2 differentiator is routing policy (round-robin vs least-loaded, a 0.55% gap), not batch size. TPE's startup trials (5 random) should hit round-robin within ~3 trials (P=1/3 per trial), but seed-dependence makes this inconsistent.
arms.diagnostic_note: The Phase 2 improvement is only 0.55% (routing: least-loaded→round-robin) vs the predicted 26% (batch 128→512). The predicted mechanism was batch-size dominance, but Phase 1 already uses batch=512, making the actual Phase 2 knob routing. TPE should theoretically learn routing faster than LHS, but with only 3 options (round-robin/least-loaded/weighted) and 5 startup trials, both converge at similar speeds. The inconsistency across seeds (TPE wins 2/3) suggests the 0.55% improvement window is too small for TPE's surrogate model to show systematic advantage at budget=50.

Key finding: extremes-first Phase 1 (4 evals) outperforms sequential Phase 1 (14-15 evals) consistently across hardware and rate conditions. h-ablation TPE vs LHS advantage is inconsistent (2/3 seeds) and the mechanism differed from prediction (routing not batch-size is the Phase 2 differentiator). RP-C2-3 requires update: 'zero effect at low rate' applies only to throughput, not composite fitness.
